Community Garden Report

The community garden opened its gates this spring after volunteers spent several months preparing the soil and repairing the old wooden fences. Families gathered on Saturday to plant vegetables and learn how to care for the shared beds.

This community garden gives residents a place to grow fresh food and meet their neighbors. Volunteers water the plants each morning and record their progress in a notebook kept beside the tool shed. Everyone can contribute time or seeds.

The organizers plan to offer workshops about composting and water conservation throughout the summer. They hope the community garden will become a lasting resource for the neighborhood and a welcoming place for people of all ages.
